mining-s1.title: A stream above and below an old mine

table.caption: Water samples from one stream, upstream and downstream of a mine that closed 40 years ago (invented data for practice)
rows: Kinds of insects found in 1 m² of stream bottom

options: The soil and rock removed from on top of a deposit
The valuable mineral that is left after the ore is processed
The water that is pumped out of a deep mine shaft
The machine that lifts ore to the top of a mine shaft

why.correct: Overburden lies above the ore and is stripped away in surface mining.
options: Right: the material above the ore.
The waste left after processing is tailings, not the mineral itself.
Pumped water is mine water, not overburden.
The structure over a shaft is a headframe.

items.q: Which is an advantage of surface mining over subsurface mining?
options: It is cheaper and safer for miners
It disturbs a smaller area of land
It produces less waste rock per ton of ore
It leaves the habitat above the deposit intact

why.correct: Surface mines avoid the cave-ins, explosions and poor air of deep mines and use big, efficient machines.
options: Right: lower cost and less danger to miners.
Surface mining disturbs much more land.
Removing overburden produces more waste.
Surface mining removes the habitat above the deposit.

items.q: How does acid mine drainage form?
options: Sulfide minerals in exposed rock react with air and water
Acidic rainwater falls on the mine and collects in the pit as acid
Miners pour acid into the mine to dissolve the ore and leave it there
Coal burned at the mine releases acid that drips into nearby streams

why.correct: Mining exposes sulfide minerals such as pyrite to oxygen and water, which form sulfuric acid.
options: Right: sulfides plus air and water make sulfuric acid.
Rain is only slightly acidic; acid mine drainage comes from the exposed rock itself.
Acid drainage forms naturally from the rock; it is not poured in.
Coal is not burned at the mine to make drainage.

items.q: In mountaintop removal, the top of a mountain is blasted away to reach coal, and the rock is dumped into nearby valleys. Which is a direct effect?
options: Valley streams are buried and the water below gets sediment and metals
The mountain gains height as the rock is piled back on top of it
More forest grows in the valleys because the rock adds nutrients
The coal seam is protected because the rock now covers it

why.correct: Valley fills bury headwater streams, and water flowing through the rubble picks up sediment and dissolved minerals.
options: Right: buried streams and polluted water downstream.
The mountain is lowered, not raised.
Rubble buries the forest and soil.
The coal is mined; the rock is removed to reach it.

items.q: As the richest copper ores are used up, mines turn to ores with less copper per ton of rock. Which effect is most likely?
options: More rock is moved and more waste is made for each kilogram of copper
Less energy is needed per kilogram of copper because the ore is softer
Less land is disturbed because the poorer ore lies closer together
Tailings piles shrink because there is less copper to remove

why.correct: Lower-grade ore means more rock to dig, crush and process per kilogram of metal, so more energy, waste and land.
options: Right: lower grade means more rock and waste.
More rock to crush means more energy, not less.
More rock means more land disturbed.
More waste rock means larger tailings piles.

items.q: In the United States, a federal law requires coal mine operators to post money before mining that is used to restore the land if they do not. Why require the money in advance?
options: So reclamation is paid for if the company goes out of business
So the mine can dig deeper without a permit later on
So the price of coal falls for people who use electricity
So the miners are paid if the mine closes early

why.correct: A bond in advance means taxpayers are not left with the cost of an abandoned mine.
options: Right: the money is there even if the company is gone.
The money is for reclamation, not for permits to dig deeper.
The aim is to restore land, not change coal prices.
The money is for land, not wages.

items.q: A copper ore contains 0.6% copper by mass. How many kilograms of ore must be mined to get 1,500 kg of copper?

why.correct: Copper is 0.6% of the ore, so ore = copper ÷ 0.006: $\frac{1{,}500\,\text{kg}}{0.6 / 100} = 250{,}000$ kg of ore.

mistakes.why: That is 0.6% of 1,500. Here 1,500 kg is the copper, which is 0.6% of the ore: divide 1,500 by 0.006.
Change 0.6% to a decimal correctly: 0.6 / 100 = 0.006, not 0.06.

items.q: A surface coal mine is closing. Describe one reclamation step and explain how it helps the land recover.

why.correct: A specific step with how it works: replacing the stored topsoil and planting native grasses gives roots and soil life back, which holds the soil and lets plants and animals return.

solution.label: Step
options: replace the saved topsoil and plant native grasses and trees
leave the pit open to fill with rainwater
pile the overburden higher in one place

why.1: An open pit can fill with acidic water and is not reclamation.
why.2: Piling waste higher leaves bare, eroding slopes.

mechanism.label: How it works
options: puts soil, roots and plant cover back on the bare ground
removes the remaining coal from the seam
raises the pH of rain

why.1: Reclamation restores land; it does not mine more.
why.2: Planting does not change the pH of rain.

effect.label: Result
options: erosion falls and plants and animals can return
erosion rises and sediment reaches streams
the mine can reopen sooner

why.2: Reclamation is not for reopening the mine.

specific.model: The company should replace the saved topsoil and plant native grasses and trees, which puts soil, roots and plant cover back on the bare ground. As a result erosion falls and plants and animals can return.

items.q: Which comparison does the table show?
options: The downstream water is more acidic and has more iron and zinc
The downstream water is less acidic and has less dissolved iron and zinc
The two samples have the same pH but different numbers of insects
The upstream water is more acidic and has more kinds of insects

why.correct: Downstream pH is 4.0 (more acidic) and iron and zinc are far higher.
options: Right: lower pH and higher metals downstream.
Downstream has a lower pH, which is more acidic, and more metal.
The pH values differ, 7.0 against 4.0.
Upstream is neutral (pH 7.0), not more acidic.

items.q: How many times more acidic (higher in hydrogen ion concentration) is the downstream water than the upstream water?

why.correct: Each pH unit is a factor of 10. The difference is $7.0 - 4.0 = 3$ units, so $10^{3} = 1{,}000$ times more acidic.

mistakes.why: 3 is the difference in pH units. Each unit is a factor of 10: 10 × 10 × 10.
pH units multiply, not add: three units is 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000, not 3 × 10.

items.q: Write the setup for the percent change in the number of kinds of insects from upstream to downstream, then give the answer.

mistakes.why: Divide by the upstream value, 22, which is the starting point.
Subtract upstream from downstream: (3 - 22). The number fell, so the change is negative.
That is the change from downstream back up to upstream. Start from upstream, 22.
-19 is the change in the number of kinds. Divide by 22 and multiply by 100.

items.q: Using the data, explain why fewer kinds of insects live downstream of the mine.

why.correct: A full chain from the data: acid drainage lowers the pH to 4.0 and carries dissolved iron and zinc; many insects cannot tolerate acid water or metals; so only 3 kinds survive instead of 22.

specific.frame: Water leaving the mine ___ and ___, so ___.

cause.label: pH
options: is acidic (pH 4.0 instead of 7.0)
is basic (pH 7.0 instead of 4.0)
has the same pH as upstream

why.1: Downstream is pH 4.0, the acidic sample.

effect.label: Metals
options: carries much more dissolved iron and zinc
carries less dissolved iron and zinc
carries no metals

why.1: Iron rises from 0.1 to 12 mg/L downstream.
why.2: Downstream water has 12 mg/L of iron and 1.5 mg/L of zinc.

mechanism.label: Effect on insects
options: many kinds of insects cannot survive, and the number of kinds falls from 22 to 3
more kinds of insects survive, so the number rises from 3 to 22
the insects are unaffected

specific.model: Water leaving the mine is acidic (pH 4.0 instead of 7.0) and carries much more dissolved iron and zinc, so many kinds of insects cannot survive, and as a result the number of kinds falls from 22 to 3.

items.q: In the diagram, where is the overburden?
options: In a pile beside the open pit
At the bottom of the vertical shaft
In the tunnel that leads to the deep ore
Under the deep ore deposit

why.correct: The overburden pile sits next to the open pit, where the material above the shallow ore was dumped.
options: Right: piled beside the pit.
The shaft leads to deep ore; no overburden is shown there.
Tunnels lead to ore, not to overburden.
Overburden lies above ore, not below it.

items.q: According to the diagram, how does acid drainage get from the mine to the water?
options: It flows from the tailings down through the ground toward the water
It falls as rain directly into the open pit from the sky above
It is pumped up the shaft of the subsurface mine by the miners
It seeps out of the deep ore through the tunnels into the air

why.correct: The arrow runs from the tailings pile down to the label "Acid drainage carries metals into water".
options: Right: from the waste pile, through the ground, to water.
The diagram does not show acid entering as rain.
No pumping is shown.
Drainage moves with water, not into the air.

items.q: A company has found ore at the depth shown on the right side of the diagram. Why would it likely choose subsurface mining?
options: The ore is too deep for removing the overburden to pay off
Subsurface mining makes more tailings, which can be sold
Subsurface mining is safer for miners than surface mining
Subsurface mining clears far more habitat on the surface

why.correct: For deep ore, removing everything above it would cost far more than the ore is worth, so shafts and tunnels are used.
options: Right: deep ore is reached more cheaply by shafts.
Tailings are waste, not a product.
Subsurface mining is more dangerous for miners.
Subsurface mining disturbs less surface habitat.

items.q: A surface mine opens above a forested valley. Which of these is a likely effect on the stream below? Select all that apply.
options: More sediment washed from bare ground into the stream
A rise in stream pH as metals are removed from the water
More forest shade over the stream
Less erosion on the slopes around the pit
Lower levels of dissolved metals in the stream

why.correct: Bare ground erodes into the stream. Mine drainage lowers pH and adds metals, and the forest is removed.
options: Right: bare ground erodes into the stream.
Mine drainage lowers pH and adds metals.
Surface mining removes forest cover and shade.
Bare slopes erode more, not less.
Mine waste adds dissolved metals.
